mn60:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kosalan country with a large Sangha of bhikkhus, and he eventually arrived at a divine-caste Kosalan village called Sālā.
mn60:2.1: The divine-caste householders of Sālā heard
mn60:3.1: Then the divine-caste householders of Sālā went to the Blessed One … (repeat Sutta 41, para. 3)… sat down at one side.
mn60:4.1: ‘Householders, have you any loved teacher in whom you have found your faith well founded ?’
mn60:4.3: ‘Then, householders, while you have no loved teacher this Incontrovertible Dhamma can be practised and maintained,
mn60:4.4: for when the Incontrovertible Dhamma has been taken up and maintained, it will be long for your welfare and happiness.
mn60:5.1: (I. The Theory That There Is Nothing)
mn60:5.2: “There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing sacrificed, no fruit or ripening of good and bad kammas, no this world, no other world, no father, no mother, no spontaneously (born) beings, no good and virtuous monks and divines that have themselves realized by direct knowledge and declared this world and the other world.”
mn60:6.1: (B) ‘Now there are some monks and divines directly opposed to those monks and divines
mn60:6.3: “There is what is given and what is offered and what is sacrificed, and there is fruit and ripening of good and bad kammas, and there is this world and the other world, and mother and father, and spontaneously (born) beings, and good and virtuous monks and divines that have themselves realized by direct knowledge and declare this world and the other world.”
mn60:6.5: do not these monks and divines hold theories directly opposed to each other ?’
mn60:7.1: ‘Now of those monks and divines whose theory and view is thus:
mn60:7.2: “There is nothing given … no good and virtuous monks and divines that have themselves realized by direct knowledge and declare this world
mn60:7.3: it is to be expected that they will avoid these three profitable dhammas, namely, bodily good conduct, verbal good conduct, mental good conduct, and that they will take to and maintain these three unprofitable dhammas, namely, bodily bad conduct, verbal bad conduct and mental bad conduct.
mn60:7.5: Because those worthy monks and divines do not see the danger, the degradation and the defilement in unprofitable dhammas, and they do not see the blessing of renunciation partaking of cleansing in profitable dhammas.
mn60:8.1: There actually being another world, one whose view is “There is not another world” has a wrong view.
mn60:8.2: There actually being another world, one whose intention is “There is not another world” has a wrong intention.
mn60:8.3: There actually being another world, one who speaks the words “There is not another world” has wrong speech.
mn60:8.4: There actually being another world, one who says “There is not another world” is directly opposed to those Arahants who know the other world.
mn60:8.5: There actually being another world, one who makes another perceive “There is not another world” makes (him) perceive what is not True Dhamma,
mn60:8.6: and in (order to) make (him) perceive what is not True Dhamma he praises himself and disparages others.
mn60:8.7: So that any virtuousness that he has is abandoned and unvirtuousness is substituted.
mn60:8.8: And this wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, opposition to Noble Ones, making (another) perceive what is not True Dhamma, and self-praise and disparagement of others—these several evil unprofitable dhammas are thus brought into positive being with wrong view as their condition.
mn60:9.1: ‘About this a wise man considers thus:
mn60:9.2: “If there is not another world, then on the dissolution of the body, this worthy person will have made himself safe enough.
mn60:9.3: But if there is another world, then on the dissolution of the body, after death, he will reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.
mn60:9.4: Now by all means let there be no other world, and let these worthy monks’ and divines’ words be true,
mn60:9.5: still this worthy person comes in for wise men’s censure here and now as ‘an unvirtuous person with wrong view and the theory that there is nothing’.
mn60:9.6: But on the other hand, if there is another world, then this worthy person has had an unlucky throw on both counts:
mn60:9.7: since he has come in for wise men’s censure here and now, and since on the dissolution of the body, after death, he will reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn60:9.8: He has wrongly taken up and practised this incontrovertible dhamma in such a way that as it extends only to one side it excludes the profitable aspects’.

mn60:13.1: ‘There are some monks and divines whose theory and whose view is thus:
mn60:13.2: “When a man acts or has action done, when he mutilates or has mutilation done, when he tortures or has torturing done, when he inflicts sorrow, when he oppresses, when he threatens or causes threatening, when he slays living beings, takes what is not given, breaks open locks for plunder, commits burglary, ambushes highways, goes with another’s wife, utters falsehood—no evil is done for the doer.
mn60:13.3: If a man with a razor-rimmed wheel makes the living beings on this earth into one mash of meat, into one heap of meat, there is no evil sourcing from it and no outcome to evil.
mn60:13.4: If a man follows the Ganges’ south bank killing and slaughtering, mutilating and having mutilation done, torturing and having torture done, there is no evil sourcing from it and no outcome of evil.
mn60:13.5: If a man follows the Ganges’ north bank giving (gifts) and having (them) given, offering (sacrifices) and having them offered, then there is no merit sourcing from it and no outcome of merit.
mn60:13.6: By giving, by training, by restraint, by speaking truth, there is no merit and no outcome of merit.”
mn60:14.1: ‘Now there are some monks and divines whose theory is directly opposed to those monks and divines, and they say thus:
mn60:14.2: “When a man acts or has action done, when he mutilates or has mutilation done, when he tortures or has torturing done, when he inflicts sorrow, when he op-presses, when he threatens or causes threatening, when he slays living beings, takes what is not given, breaks open locks, raids for plunder, commits burglary, ambushes highways, goes with another’s wife, utters falsehood—evil is done for the doer.
mn60:14.3: If a man with a razor-rimmed wheel makes the living beings on this earth into one mash of meat, into one heap of meat, there is evil sourcing from it and there is outcome of evil.
mn60:14.4: If a man follows the Ganges’ south bank killing and slaughtering, mutilating and having mutilation done, torturing and having torture done, there is evil sourcing from it, and outcome of evil.
mn60:14.5: If a man follows the Ganges’ north bank giving (gifts) and having (them) given, offering (sacrifices) and having (them) offered, there is merit sourcing from it, and outcome of merit.
mn60:14.6: By giving, by training, by restraint, by speaking truth, there is merit, and outcome of merit.”
mn60:14.8: do not these monks and divines hold theories directly opposed to each other?’

mn60:21.1: There are some monks and divines whose theory and whose view is thus:
mn60:21.2: “There is no reason, no condition, for beings’ defilement;
mn60:21.3: beings are defiled without reason or condition.
mn60:21.4: There is no reason, no condition for beings’ purification;
mn60:21.5: beings are purified without reason or condition.
mn60:21.6: There is no power, no energy, no manly courage, no manly endurance;
mn60:21.7: all creatures, all breathing things, all beings, all souls, are without mastery, power or energy; moulded by fate, coincidence and essence, they experience pleasure and pain in the six species.”
mn60:22.1: Now there are some monks and divines whose theory is directly opposed to those monks and divines,
mn60:22.3: “There is a reason, a condition, for beings’ defilement;
mn60:22.4: beings are defiled owing to a reason, owing to a condition.
mn60:22.5: There is a reason, a condition, for beings’ purification;
mn60:22.6: beings are purified owing to a reason, owing to a condition.
mn60:22.7: There is power, energy, manly courage, manly endurance;
mn60:22.8: that all creatures, all breathing things, all beings, all souls, being moulded by fate, coincidence and essence, experience pleasure and pain in the six species is not so.”’
mn60:22.10: do not these monks and divines hold theories directly opposed to each other?’
mn60:23.1: ‘Now of those monks and divines whose theory and view is thus:

mn60:31.1: ‘About this a wise man considers thus:
mn60:31.2: “When these worthy monks and divines hold the theory and the view that
mn60:31.3: ‘There definitely are no formless states’, that has not been seen by me;
mn60:31.4: and when these (other) worthy monks and divines hold the theory and view that
mn60:31.5: ‘There definitely are formless states’, that has not been known by me.
mn60:31.6: If I, not seeing and not knowing, were to take one side entirely (saying)
mn60:31.7: ‘Only this is true; anything else is wrong’, that would not become me.
mn60:31.8: Not if the monks’ and divines’ theory and view that
mn60:31.9: ‘There definitely are no formless states’ is true, then it is still possible incontrovertibly that my reappearance (after death) might take place among the formed gods consisting of mind;
mn60:31.10: my reappearance (after death) might take place among the formed gods consisting of mind;
mn60:31.11: but if the monks’ and divines’ theory and view that
mn60:31.12: ‘There definitely are formless states’ is true, then it is also possible incontrovertibly that
mn60:31.13: my reappearance (after death) might take place among the formless gods consisting of perception.
mn60:31.14: (What has to be considered is that) resorting to sticks, resorting to weapons, quarrels, brawls, disputes, recriminations, malice, and false speech is to be seen regarding form
mn60:31.15: but definitely there is not this about formless states.”
mn60:31.16: After reflecting thus, he practises the way to dispassion, fading out and cessation, of forms only (but not of being).

mn60:56.2: not being interested in self-torture, and he does not torment others, not being interested in torturing others; since he torments neither himself nor others he is here, now unparched, extinguished, cooled, he abides experiencing pleasure as one become divine in himself.
mn60:57.1: When this was said, the divine-caste householders of Sālā said:
